a.onclick: openModal( this, "Infectious Diseases (CHIKV)", ["31101672","34887572"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31101672","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34887572"], ["mRNA-encoded antibodies can provide rapid passive immunization against infectious diseases by enabling in vivo production of neutralizing antibodies shortly after administration, potentially replacing repeated recombinant antibody dosing.","The clinical proof-of-concept is mRNA-1944 (encoding the anti-chikungunya antibody CHKV-24): a single intravenous LNP-mRNA infusion produced neutralising antibody at therapeutically relevant titres in a first-in-human phase 1 trial."])

openModal( this, "Cancer Immunotherapy", ["38448606","37860278"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38448606","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37860278"], ["T cell-engaging bispecific antibodies simultaneously bind a tumor-associated antigen and CD3 on T lymphocytes, promoting immune synapse formation and selective tumor cell killing independently of peptide–MHC recognition.","mRNA-encoded antibodies are now entering oncology in several formats: for example, BNT141 delivers mRNA encoding the anti-Claudin-18.2 IgG1 antibody zolbetuximab, which the liver translates and secretes to target CLDN18.2-positive solid tumours (a conventional monoclonal antibody rather than a T-cell engager)."])

openModal( this, "LNPs mainly trafficked to the liver", ["37860278"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37860278"], ["Lipid nanoparticles protect mRNA from enzymatic degradation and facilitate intracellular delivery. After systemic administration, LNPs are preferentially taken up by hepatocytes through apolipoprotein E-mediated interactions, where endosomal escape releases the mRNA into the cytoplasm for translation."])

openModal( this, "mRNA-Encoded Antibody Development", ["33572679"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33572679"], ["Unlike recombinant antibodies, mRNA therapeutics deliver the genetic instructions encoding the antibody rather than the protein itself. Following sequence design and in vitro transcription, the mRNA is encapsulated into lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), allowing rapid manufacturing and significantly shortening development timelines while maintaining the same antibody sequence."])

openModal( this, "mRNA-LNP design", ["40822034"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40822034"], ["An mRNA therapeutic contains several functional elements, including the 5′ cap, untranslated regions, coding sequence and poly(A) tail, that collectively regulate stability, translation efficiency and protein expression."])

openModal( this, "Heavy and Light Chains Encoded by Two mRNAs", ["33572679"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33572679"], ["One strategy delivers separate mRNAs encoding the heavy and light antibody chains. Both transcripts are translated independently and the resulting polypeptides assemble intracellularly into a functional antibody."])

openModal( this, "Heavy and Light Chains Encoded by One mRNA", ["33572679"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33572679"], ["Alternatively, a single mRNA can encode both antibody chains separated by self-cleaving peptides such as P2A. This approach ensures coordinated expression from one transcript while simplifying manufacturing."])

openModalLink( this, "The modules can be combined in many ways to create functional Ab", ["35868279"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35868279"], [["Variable regions, hinges and constant domains are modular building blocks that can be re-organized and engineered to generate virtually any antibody format, from full-length IgGs and antibody fragments to Fc-fusion proteins, bispecifics and multispecifics. By tuning valency, specificity, size, half-life and effector function, the format can be tailored to the intended clinical application and indication.","https://absoluteantibody.com/periodic-table-of-antibodies/","Periodic Table of antibodies."]])

openModal( this, "2+1 T-cell Engager", ["37861452"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37861452"], ["A 2+1 T-cell engager (TCE) is an asymmetric bispecific antibody containing two antigen-binding domains directed against a tumor-associated antigen and one binding domain targeting CD3 on T lymphocytes. The bivalent interaction with the tumor increases avidity and preferential retention on cancer cells, while the monovalent CD3 arm recruits and activates T cells only after tumor binding. This design enhances tumor selectivity and may reduce systemic T-cell activation and cytokine release compared with conventional 1+1 T-cell engagers."])

openModal( this, "Unmodified vs Modified mRNA", ["41521363"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41521363"], ["Naturally occurring uridine residues can activate innate immune receptors and reduce translation efficiency. Substituting uridine with modified nucleosides such as N1-methylpseudouridine decreases innate immune activation, increases protein expression and prolongs mRNA stability, making modified mRNAs the preferred platform for most therapeutic applications."])

openModal( this, "Fc Region", ["37371712"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37371712"], ["The Fc region mediates interactions with Fcγ receptors and complement proteins, thereby regulating antibody half-life and immune effector mechanisms such as antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC)."])

openModal( this, "Fab region", ["37371712"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37371712"], ["The Fab (fragment antigen binding) region contains the variable domains responsible for antigen recognition. Sequence diversity within the complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) determines antibody specificity."])

openModal( this, "Hepatocyte (biofactory)", ["41521363"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41521363"], ["After intravenous administration, hepatocytes function as temporary in vivo bioreactors, continuously producing therapeutic antibodies for several days before mRNA degradation terminates protein expression."])

openModal( this, "mRNA Translation", ["40822034"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40822034"], ["Once released into the cytoplasm, the mRNA is translated by ribosomes into antibody polypeptide chains. Translation efficiency is regulated by the 5′ cap, untranslated regions (UTRs), codon optimization and poly(A) tail length."])

openModal( this, "Signal Peptide", ["38143019"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38143019"], ["The N-terminal signal peptide directs the nascent antibody chain to the rough endoplasmic reticulum, where co-translational translocation initiates the secretory pathway. The signal peptide is subsequently cleaved before antibody maturation."])

openModal( this, "Protein Folding", ["38143019","35416297"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38143019","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35416297"], ["Within the endoplasmic reticulum, molecular chaperones assist antibody folding and ensure the correct formation of intramolecular and intermolecular disulfide bonds required for structural stability.","Because the antibody is produced in the patient’s own cells, it also acquires human-type glycosylation, which can reduce the risk of anti-drug antibody (ADA) responses relative to proteins made in non-human production cell lines."])

openModal( this, "Secretion via Golgi", ["38143019"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38143019"], ["Following folding and assembly, antibodies are transported through the Golgi apparatus and secreted into the bloodstream by the producing hepatocyte, where they can distribute systemically and reach distant target tissues."])

openModal( this, "Endosomal Escape", ["38437552"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38437552"], ["Following cellular uptake, lipid nanoparticles become trapped within endosomes. Ionizable lipids acquire a positive charge in the acidic endosomal environment, destabilizing the membrane and promoting endosomal escape, a critical step that determines the efficiency of mRNA translation."])

openModal( this, "Antibody Assembly", ["38143019"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38143019"], ["Heavy and light chains assemble through disulfide bond formation to generate the mature immunoglobulin structure. Correct assembly is required for antigen recognition and Fc-mediated effector functions."])

openModal( this, "Bispecific Antibodies", ["38448606"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38448606"], ["Bispecific antibodies simultaneously recognize two different antigens or epitopes, enabling mechanisms such as immune cell redirection, dual receptor blockade or enhanced target selectivity."])

openModalLink( this, "Serum Antibody Concentration Over Time", ["36403209"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36403209"], [["Unlike recombinant antibodies, which reach their maximum serum concentration immediately after administration, mRNA therapeutics require an initial protein expression phase. Antibody concentration therefore increases gradually before reaching a delayed peak and subsequently declines as mRNA expression decreases and antibody clearance predominates. As a result, their pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles are very different.","https://advanced.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/cms/asset/6e7ead95-2aef-4c7d-a420-f3a67e691894/advs4743-fig-0005-m.jpg","Panel F displays the concentration-time profile in mice of the B7H3-redirected Bispecific Antibody in its recombinant and mRNA-encoded form. The PK profiles show distinct behaviors: the recombinant antibody (blue) is injected in the blood stream and is gradually cleared, while for the mRNA-encoded antibody (red) there’s a first ramp up phase, accounting for mRNA escape and translation, with a clearance that is present but masked by the antibody production that lasts days inside the hepatocytes."]])

openModal( this, "Recombinant Antibody Development", ["41521363"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41521363"], ["Recombinant monoclonal antibodies are traditionally developed by identifying a therapeutic target, engineering antibody-producing cell lines and manufacturing the protein in large-scale bioreactors. This process requires extensive optimization, purification and quality control, resulting in development timelines that typically span several months to years before clinical use."])

openModal( this, "Programmable Antibody Platform", ["41521363"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41521363"], ["Messenger RNA provides a programmable platform for the rapid in vivo production of virtually any antibody format. By simply changing the coding sequence, the same manufacturing process can generate conventional monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies, multispecific antibodies or engineered Fc-containing molecules without modifying the delivery technology. This flexibility enables rapid adaptation to different therapeutic applications, including cancer, infectious diseases and autoimmune disorders."])

openModal( this, "Fc-Fusion Proteins", ["36726033"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36726033"], ["Fc-fusion proteins combine the Fc region of an immunoglobulin with a therapeutic protein, peptide or receptor domain. The Fc portion prolongs serum half-life through neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn)-mediated recycling and can improve protein stability, solubility and pharmacokinetic properties."])

openModal( this, "Monoclonal Antibodies (mAbs)", ["37371712"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37371712"], ["Monoclonal antibodies recognize a single epitope on a target antigen through two identical antigen-binding sites. Their high specificity allows selective neutralization of soluble mediators, receptor blockade or targeted elimination of diseased cells, making them one of the most widely used therapeutic protein classes."])

openModal( this, "Hexabody antigen-induced IgG hexamer", ["35235843"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35235843"], ["Hexameric antibodies are engineered to assemble into higher-order Fc oligomers that increase functional avidity and enhance complement activation through improved C1q recruitment. These molecules are being investigated for applications requiring stronger immune effector functions than conventional IgG antibodies."])
